extraction_scope: Worker-6 final source-reviewed mechanism adjudication from primary results, figure captions/images, and methods; automated pending-review mechanism placeholders were replaced with paper-specific claims.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Yodha directly disrupts ZIKV virion morphology after short peptide exposure, consistent with virucidal particle damage rather than only post-entry inhibition.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=7:Yodha disrupts Zika virus integrity; fig=3

mechanism_claims.limitations: TEM supports physical disruption/aggregation of ZIKV particles; it does not identify the exact molecular binding site on the virion.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Pre-exposure of ZIKV to Yodha reduces subsequent viral RNA entry signal in Vero cells and decreases detectable envelope staining.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=6:Yodha peptide can reduce viral titers and limit the spread of ZIKV in vitro; fig=2B-D

mechanism_claims.limitations: The entry assay is downstream of virion preincubation; it supports loss of entry competence but does not by itself distinguish binding from particle disruption without the TEM evidence.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Structure-activity observations map improved activity to the N-terminal hydrophobic region and support a membrane/lipid-bilayer destabilization hypothesis.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=9:Naturally occurring variants of Yodha are also effective against ZIKV infection; discussion

mechanism_claims.limitations: This is SAR and discussion-level inference, not a direct binding-site assay.

caution_findings.evidence_context: The article explicitly leaves the precise ZIKV particle region targeted by Yodha unresolved.
